title: India Notifies First New Zealand FTA Duty Cuts, Sheep Meat at Zero From October 20
excerpt: The October 16 customs notification sets preferential rates for sheep meat, kiwi fruit, fish, wine and manuka honey from October 20, while New Zealand opens all 8,284 tariff lines to Indian goods duty-free.
body:
• India has notified the first customs duty concessions under its free trade agreement with New Zealand, with preferential rates taking effect on October 20.
  • Fresh, chilled and frozen sheep meat from New Zealand will enter India at zero basic customs duty, while eligible kiwi fruit priced at $2.50 per kg or more will attract 15% duty.
  • New Zealand will remove duties on all 8,284 of its tariff lines for Indian goods from day one, and has committed $20 billion in investment in India over 15 years.
  • Importers must prove New Zealand origin and meet tariff-rate quota conditions to claim the cuts; dairy and other sensitive farm products stay outside the concessions.

India has notified the first set of customs duty concessions for imports from New Zealand under the two countries' free trade agreement, setting preferential rates that take effect on October 20. The Finance Ministry notification, issued on October 16 by the Department of Revenue under the Customs Act, 1962, lists revised basic customs duty and cess rates for designated tariff lines, according to Mint's report of the notification.

What Gets Cheaper, and on What Terms

The headline change is sheep meat. Fresh, chilled and frozen sheep meat covered by the specified tariff entry will attract zero basic customs duty, zero Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess and zero health cess — down from a duty of about 30% before the agreement. Eligible kiwi fruit valued at $2.50 per kg or more will be charged at 15%. Certain fish products listed under specified tariff lines will attract basic customs duty of 25.71%, with cess set at zero, on a path that phases down over the coming years. Wine and manuka honey are also covered by the preferential framework, with rates governed by their tariff entries and quota conditions.

The concessions are not a blanket opening. Access runs through tariff-rate quotas, which allow specified quantities of eligible products to enter at preferential rates, and importers must establish New Zealand origin and satisfy product-specific conditions before claiming a lower rate. Dairy products and key agricultural items remain outside the concessions, a protection India held through the negotiations for its farm sector.

The Other Side of the Deal

For Indian exporters, the agreement is broader. New Zealand will eliminate duties on all 8,284 of its tariff lines for Indian goods from day one, covering textiles, apparel, leather, footwear, engineering goods, chemicals and pharmaceuticals. India's own offer covers about 70% of its tariff lines and roughly 95% of the value of New Zealand's exports to India, with about 30% of lines moving to zero immediately and a further tranche phasing to zero over three to ten years. A second tranche of Indian concessions arrives on January 1, 2027.

The pact was signed on April 27, 2026, by Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal and New Zealand Trade Minister Todd McClay after talks that ran from March to December 2025. New Zealand's Parliament approved the deal on September 16 by 93 votes to 29, and both countries exchanged ratification documents ahead of the October 20 start, according to reporting on the ratification. McClay said 57% of New Zealand exports to India will be tariff-free from day one, rising to 82% at full implementation, with more than 95% of forestry and wood exports duty-free.

"The New Zealand-India FTA will level the playing field and unlock access for Kiwi businesses in one of the fastest growing markets in the world."

— Todd McClay, New Zealand Trade and Investment Minister

Why It Matters Now

Two-way trade was worth about $2.3 billion in the year to June 2026, and Prime Ministers Narendra Modi and Christopher Luxon have committed to doubling bilateral trade by 2030. Wellington has also agreed to invest $20 billion in India over the next 15 years, and the agreement eases mobility rules for Indian students and workers. The deal lands as New Delhi accelerates trade agreements — including with Britain and the European Union — to diversify export markets while United States tariff policy, including a law allowing tariffs of up to 100% on countries buying Russian oil, squeezes India's largest market.

For shoppers and businesses, the practical test starts on October 20: importers who can document origin and fit within quota limits will see landed costs fall on sheep meat immediately, while kiwi fruit, apples and manuka honey move through quota channels with price floors. Exporters, meanwhile, gain duty-free entry to New Zealand across every tariff line from the same date.
